full_judgment:
This revision by the defendant calls in to examine the propriety of the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.9.87 passed in Title Appeal No. 96 of 1984 by the District Judge Gopalganj, dismissing the appeal and upholding the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 1.982 by the Subordinate Judge, Gopalganj decreeing the suit by his judgment and decree dated 27.6.84 declaring that two registered kabalas selling the suit property are illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff and the plaintiff is the Shebait of the Suit Property. 

 4. The defendants 1-3 have been contesting the suit by filing a joint written statements in denial of the case of the plaintiff and contending, inter alia, that since the plaintiff has set up new deities in the suit land it has lost its character as debutter property. The plaintiff has no locus standi to file the suit as shebait. The endowment is not a public one. It is a private and secular one, not acted upon, and as such, is heritable and consequently the defendants 7 and 8 inherited the suit property and transferred the same to the defendants 1-3 legally. The trial Court decreed the suit. On appeal by the contesting defendants the judgment and decree of the trial Court has been upheld and the appeal has been dismissed. Against the same the instant revision has been preferred by the said contesting defendants. 

 Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record my considered view is that the Courts below committed no error of law in decreeing the suit resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Thus the judgment and decree of the Courts below cannot be upset. Therefore, the result is, that the Rule is discharged with costs.
